paragraphs: Two outbreaks linked to contaminated foods have ended.[1][2] An E. coli O26 outbreak associated with raw milk cheese affected 18 people across 10 states, with 9 hospitalizations and no deaths.[1] A separate outbreak involving E. coli and Salmonella linked to alfalfa sprouts sickened 77 people across 16 states, resulting in 6 hospitalizations and no deaths.[2]

Family Farmstead Dairy has recalled all cheddar cheese products due to potential Listeria monocytogenes contamination, which can cause serious infections in young children, elderly people, and those with weakened immune systems.[3] Fresh & Ready Foods LLC is recalling Fresh To You brand Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwiches for the same reason.[4] Country Creek LLC and Francisco Family Foods have recalled sprouting seeds sold under the Country Creek Acres and Francisco Family Foods brands because of possible E. coli and Salmonella contamination.[19]

An E. coli outbreak is ongoing at Ohio University, with 11 confirmed cases among students as of November 14.[6] Oysters from Little Wicomico Oyster Company in Virginia continue to test positive for Salmonella in multiple samples.[16]
